params.body:
**Triage proposal** (from the forwarded mail; change the labels if it is wrong)
Category: bug  Priority: P2
Summary: Two vehicles that came in through Hexon have a valid Car-Pass, and Hexon now sends its URL, but the platform still shows them as "to register". The dealer's own registration attempt on 2026-10-31 came back four times as "Probleem gemeld". The dealer cannot get these cars marked as having a Car-Pass.

Source: Portal mail:38. The vehicles and the garage are named there and are left out here.

## What is reported

One garage imports its stock from AutoScout24 into Hexon, and Hexon sends it to the platform. Three of its vehicles show Car-Pass as "to register":

- For one vehicle Hexon never sent a Car-Pass URL, so "to register" is correct.
- For the other two, the Hexon admin now shows a Car-Pass URL (`public.car-pass.be/vhr/...`) in the data it sends. The vehicles were created on 2026-08-13, before the migration. Nobody can tell whether the URL was in that first delivery or added later.
- On 2026-10-31 the dealer tried to register both from the platform. Every attempt shows "Probleem gemeld" in the Car-Pass history on the sheet. Car-Pass itself shows the registration as done in the dealer's account.

## What the code shows

**A Car-Pass URL that comes after the vehicle was created is dropped for most dealers.** `main.carpass` is stored in `vehicles.carpass_id` in two cases only:

- when the API creates the vehicle (`VehicleApiService::storeVehicle`, which also sets `carpass_init`);
- when the API updates it (`VehicleApiController::update`).

`update` refuses every caller whose dealer is not a premium trader (`type != 1`) and answers `update-method temporary unavailable` (R P3-1.11). `store` on an existing vehicle gives the same refusal (`vehicle already found in system`). The refused data is kept as a proposal only behind the `partner_proposals` flag, and that flag is on for one garage. So for any other non-premium dealer, a Car-Pass URL that Hexon adds after the first delivery never reaches the vehicle, and there is no error and no trace. The 2026-08-13 creation predates the migration, and `api_log` keeps five days, so the platform cannot show which of these two cases happened.

**The registration on 2026-10-31.** The chip means that Car-Pass answered the observation with ISSUE or ERROR (`CarpassIssue`, R S3-3.9). The raw answer of each step is in `carpass_requests` (`data`, `issues[0]`), so the issue id is in production and not in this report. Two ids fit what the dealer describes:

- 123: "already delivered a mileage for this vehicle on this date" (R S3-3.2), if the dealer registered the same car in their Car-Pass account on 2026-10-31 with the same credentials;
- 001: the mileage is lower than the last known one (R S3-8.3), if the mileage on the sheet is behind the one registered at Car-Pass.

Neither is a fault of the platform. In both, the car already has a valid Car-Pass, and the platform offers no way to attach it.

## What is needed

1. Read the issue id of the 2026-10-31 steps for the two vehicles in `carpass_requests`. That tells whether the platform did anything wrong.
2. Decide whether a partner's Car-Pass URL should be stored even when the partner may not update the vehicle otherwise. It is not a price, and the dealer's own Car-Pass account already holds the registration. If yes, store `main.carpass` on a refused update and on a refused store-on-existing (with `carpass_init`, without a new registration), and keep the rest of R P3-1.11 as it is.
3. Until then, the two vehicles can have their `carpass_id` set to the URLs that Hexon now sends (the URLs are in Portal mail:38).
params.title: Car-Pass URL sent by Hexon after creation is dropped; dealer cannot register the car again
